outcome: Pelvic floor trauma (levator ani muscle avulsion)
Anal sphincter trauma (obstetric anal sphincter injury - OASI)
cohort: The study included 201 primiparous women who had an assisted vaginal delivery and a control group of 43 primiparous women who had a normal vaginal delivery.
finding: Forceps delivery was identified as a major risk factor for levator ani muscle avulsion and was associated with a non-significantly higher risk of OASI compared to normal vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Forceps delivery showed a significantly higher rate of levator ani muscle avulsion (60%) compared to normal vaginal delivery (20.9%) and vacuum extraction (21.7%), and a non-significantly higher risk of OASI.
